name: Basthorst Castle
region: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — Basthorst, near Crivitz, between Schwerin and the Glambecksee
architectural_style: 1823 manor house (Herrenhaus) of the Schack family, within a much larger spa-hotel complex added later
accessibility: A large spa hotel spread across three separate buildings within an English-style park; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: An 1823 manor house survives at the heart of the estate — but only 19 of the hotel's 92 rooms are actually inside it; the rest are in two later, separate buildings
highlights: Manor house of 1823 built by the Schack family, today the historic core of a much larger spa and conference hotel between Schwerin and the Glambecksee

Of 92 total rooms and suites, only 19 are within the original 1823 Herrenhaus — 47 are in the separate Waldresidenz (forest wing with wellness access) and the remainder in the Turmhaus, a former administrative building set apart by a stand of trees
A 1,300m² spa and wellness area, restaurant "Wilhelmina Helena," and a grand ballroom in the Waldresidenz
Set within an English-style park on the Glambecksee, roughly midway between Hamburg and Berlin
description:
Schloss Basthorst was built in 1823 by the Schack family as a stately manor house, or Herrenhaus, set amid the rolling hills and lake landscape of western Mecklenburg. Its protected monument-status building anchors a much larger estate that later grew to include a separate administrative tower house — the Turmhaus, erected roughly fifty years after the main house and deliberately set apart from it by a stand of trees — reflecting the practical, working character of a 19th-century Mecklenburg estate rather than a single fortified residence.

Today the historic manor forms only one part of a much larger hotel complex. Alongside the original Herrenhaus, the estate now includes the Waldresidenz, a large forest-set building added later to house the wellness area, ballroom and restaurant, giving Schloss Basthorst its present identity as a spa and conference hotel rather than a boutique stay inside a single historic building. The English-style castle park and the Glambecksee lake remain the estate's most enduring historic landscape features.

It's worth stating the room split plainly: of the 92 total rooms and suites across the property, only 19 — roughly one in five — are within the 1823 Herrenhaus itself. The remaining 73 rooms are split between the Waldresidenz (47 rooms, directly connected to the spa) and the Turmhaus (the balance), both genuinely separate buildings on the estate rather than wings of the historic manor. Guests specifically seeking the manor-house experience should confirm a Herrenhaus room at booking rather than assume any room on the property offers it.

The practice of expanding a historic manor's hotel capacity through purpose-built later additions, rather than new construction squeezed into the original building, is a pattern shared by several larger spa and conference-oriented castle-hotels in this collection, where guest volume and modern wellness facilities require considerably more space than a single 19th-century house could accommodate.

Basthorst's position roughly midway between Hamburg and Berlin, with Schwerin — the state capital of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — just 25 minutes away, gives the estate a genuinely convenient location for business travelers and conference groups, a role reflected in its extensive meeting and coworking facilities alongside the spa.

The estate's English-style park, with its mature trees and lakeside setting on the Glambecksee, predates much of the later hotel expansion and remains one of the property's most consistently historic features, offering guests a genuine sense of the 19th-century estate's original landscaped grounds regardless of which building they sleep in.

Schwerin Castle (Schweriner Schloss), one of Germany's most recognizable romantic-era palace silhouettes, sits on its own lake island roughly 25 minutes from Basthorst, giving guests staying at the estate an easy and rewarding half-day pairing between a working spa hotel and one of Mecklenburg's grandest historic residences.

Western Mecklenburg's dense concentration of lakes, of which the Glambecksee is one relatively modest example, reflects the region's glacially shaped landscape, formed as retreating ice sheets carved out the numerous basins that now define much of the state's rural character — a geological backdrop shared by the wider Mecklenburg Lake District further east.
history: Schloss Basthorst was built in 1823 by the Schack family as a manor house between Schwerin and the Glambecksee. A separate administrative tower house, the Turmhaus, was added roughly fifty years later, set apart from the main house by a stand of trees. The estate has since grown into a large spa and conference hotel: of its 92 total rooms, only 19 are within the original 1823 Herrenhaus, with the remaining 73 split between the Waldresidenz (a later forest-set building with wellness access) and the Turmhaus.

faqs.question: Are most of the rooms at Basthorst Castle inside the historic manor house?
faqs.answer: No — of 92 total rooms and suites, only 19 are within the original 1823 Herrenhaus. The remaining 73 rooms are split between the Waldresidenz (47 rooms, a separate forest-set building with wellness access) and the Turmhaus, a former administrative building set apart by trees.

faqs.question: Can I request a room specifically in the historic Herrenhaus?
faqs.answer: Yes, but availability is limited to 19 rooms out of 92 total — specify the Herrenhaus explicitly when booking if sleeping in the original 1823 manor house is the priority.

faqs.question: What is at Basthorst Castle besides the historic manor?
faqs.answer: A 1,300m² spa and wellness area with pool and sauna, the restaurant "Wilhelmina Helena," a grand ballroom in the Waldresidenz, extensive conference facilities, and an English-style park on the Glambecksee lake.

meta_description: Stay at Basthorst Castle near Schwerin — an 1823 manor house at the heart of a large spa and conference hotel, on the Glambecksee lake.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The English park and the area around the Schlosssee are partly accessible to non-guests; the main building, spa and restaurant are for hotel guests and restaurant patrons only.
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** ~25 minutes by car from Schwerin (state capital of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern); roughly 1h45 from Hamburg and 2h30 from Berlin by car. No direct train to Basthorst; nearest stations are in Crivitz or Schwerin, from which a taxi or transfer is needed.

**Rooms & rates:** 92 rooms and suites spread across three buildings — 19 in the historic 1823 manor house, 47 in the Waldresidenz (forest wing with wellness access), and the rest in the Turmhaus. From €89/night; rates vary significantly by building.

**On-site:** 1,300 m² spa and wellness area with pool, sauna and treatments; restaurant "Wilhelmina Helena"; castle lounge and library with winter garden; grand ballroom; coworking lounge; extensive meeting/conference facilities.

**Good to know:** Only the original Herrenhaus is the true 19th-century manor; guests wanting the most "castle-like" experience should ask specifically for a room in that building rather than the Waldresidenz or Turmhaus.

**Combine with:** Schwerin Castle (Schweriner Schloss) is roughly 25 minutes away and makes for an easy half-day visit combined with a stay at Basthorst.
